[[Til Konnakol og Indien|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Indien]]","huwiki-text-en":"Three spoken subdivisions: ''Ta–ki–ta''. The tempo indicates a practice pulse, but these groups are not inherently tied to a 3/8 meter. First speak and clap, then fit the group into a 4/4 pulse.

<div class="huw-music-kicker">MUSIKLABORATORIUM · VERDENS RYTMER</div>
<h1>Indien · sig rytmen,<br>spil melodien.</h1>
<p class="huw-music-lead">Konnakol og solkattu er sydindiske rytmestavelser. Man taler eller synger rytmiske figurer, mens hænderne fastholder en tala. Her kan du høre originale ABC-øvelser, læse stavelserne under noderne og lave egne kompositioner.</p>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>1 · Rytmernes byggesten</h2>
<p>[[Ta-ki-ta · 3|Konnakol – Ta Ki Ta · 3]] · [[Ta-ka-di-mi · 4|Konnakol – Ta Ka Di Mi · 4]] · [[Ta-din-gi-na-tom · 5|Konnakol – Ta Din Gi Na Tom · 5]] · [[Ta-ki-ta + Ta-ka-di-mi · 7|Konnakol – Ta Ki Ta Ta Ka Di Mi · 7]]</p>
<p>''Skriv og sig stavelserne selv!'' ABC-afspilleren afspiller rytmetoner, ikke en syntetisk menneskestemme. Betoning og udtale lærer vi bedst af videoer og levende musikere.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>2 · Sæt grupperne sammen</h2>
<p>[[3+5 over en 4/4-puls|Konnakol – 3 plus 5 over fire slag]] · [[Miśra Cāpu · 7/8 melodi med becifringer|Konnakol – Miśra Cāpu · 7/8 melodi]]</p>
<p>Grupperne kan placeres i en fast tala og ændres uden at ændre grundpulsen. Læreren kan lade eleven klappe, synge og senere notere sin egen variant.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>3 · Melodier og akkompagnement</h2>
<p>[[Mohanam-inspireret melodi i Ādi-tāla|Indien – Mohanam-inspireret · Adi tala]] · [[Rūpaka-inspireret tre-slags melodi|Indien – Rupaka · tre pulsslag]]</p>
<p>Vælg de nye <strong>Indien-inspirerede undervisningsstilarter</strong> i Akkompagnement. De er bevidst MIDI-baserede modeller, ikke autentiske indiske instrumentoptagelser. De vestlige akkordsymboler er til sammenligning og komposition.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>4 · Ragaer gennem døgnet</h2>
<p>Nordindisk hindustansk musik forbinder traditionelt bestemte ragaer med tider på dagen; sydindisk konnakol og tala bygger på en anden undervisningstradition.</p>
<p>[[Mød Bhairav om morgenen og Yaman om aftenen|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Raga]]</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel">
<h2>Lyt og se rigtige udøvere</h2>
<p><strong>Konnakol-duet – V Shivapriya og BR Somashekar Jois</strong>. Hør stavelsesfraser og se, hvordan hænderne markerer en cyklisk puls.</p>
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/iurhjlBum0o" title="Konnakol duet – MadRasana Unplugged" width="560" height="315" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="max-width:100%;border:0;aspect-ratio:16/9"></iframe>
<p>[[Åbn videoen på YouTube|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iurhjlBum0o]] – virker også, hvis indlejring er blokeret i en lokal iPad-/Quine-visning.</p>
<p><strong>Raga Yaman – introduktion af Bidisha Ghosh</strong>. En nordindisk melodisk lektion, adskilt fra det sydindiske Konnakol-forløb.</p>
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/FTXP7niGcOs" title="Raga Yaman – introduktion med Bidisha Ghosh" width="560" height="315" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="max-width:100%;border:0;aspect-ratio:16/9"></iframe>
<p>[[Åbn Yaman-video på YouTube|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FTXP7niGcOs]]</p>
</div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>Opgave: Fra rytme til egen melodi</h2>
<ol><li>Lyt til en udøver, og sig stavelserne med.</li><li>Klap grundpulsen, mens du spiller rytmeøvelsen.</li><li>Lav en kopi af ABC-tiddleren, og ændr 3+5 til 5+3.</li><li>Prøv en melodi med den ønskede rytme og få klaviaturet frem.</li><li>Skriv en kort øvelseslog, og publicér eventuelt din egen udgave som en HUWiki Site-afspiller.</li></ol>
</div>
<nav class="huw-music-bottomnav">[[Musik Edition|HUWiki Musik – Start]] · [[Rytmik|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Rytmik]] · [[Ragaer|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Raga]] · [[Biblioteker|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Indiske kilder]]</nav></div>

<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>Drone · din egen Sa</h2><p>I afspilleren kan du starte en selvstændig drone, også når akkompagnementet er slået fra. Vælg Sa, Sa–Pa eller Sa–Ma, tilpas toneart, klang og lydstyrke i mixeren. Dronen bliver liggende, selv når becifringerne skifter. Vælg <strong>Stop drone</strong> for at afslutte.</p><p>Tanpura- og shruti-klangene er syntetiske pædagogiske tilnærmelser. Musikeksemplerne anvender ligeledes General MIDI-instrumenter; tabla-rytmer er ikke autentiske tabla-samples.</p></div>

!!! Instrumentering · musikalske principper (v0.3.10)

I traditionel indisk klassisk musik spilles melodien typisk over en fast ''Sa'' (eventuelt med ''Pa'' eller ''Ma'') og en rytmisk cyklus (//tāla//). De indiske studieakkompagnementer har derfor ''ingen vestlig bas eller skiftende akkorder som standard''. Klangene er kun pædagogiske synteser og GM-tilnærmelser; en ægte tanpura, shruti box, tabla eller mridangam lyder langt rigere.

''Tanpura'': plukkede strenge og harmoniske overtoner, typisk Pa–Sa–Sa–Sa. ''Shruti box'': lille luftdrevet bælginstrument med metaltunger, der holder Sa/Pa eller Sa/Ma. ''Mridangam'': sydindisk tromme til Carnatic, Ādi-tāla og konnakol. ''Tabla'': primært nordindisk tromme. Harmonium kan spille en understøttende melodilinje; det er ikke automatisk en vestlig akkordmaskine.

Når du vil prøve ''vestlig harmonisering'', kan du vælge den udtrykkelige fusionstil eller //Egen blanding//. Dronen selv ændrer ikke Sa ved akkordskift og stopper, når du trykker Stop eller vælger et nyt nodeark.
","huwiki-text-en":"<div class="huw-music-home huw-music-workshop">
<div class="huw-music-kicker">MUSIC LAB · WORLD RHYTHMS</div>
<h1>India · speak the rhythm,<br>play the melody.</h1>
<p class="huw-music-lead">Konnakol and solkattu are South Indian rhythmic syllable traditions. Musicians speak or sing rhythmic patterns while the hands keep a tāla cycle. Explore original ABC exercises, read the syllables below the notes and compose your own music.</p>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>1 · Building blocks of rhythm</h2>
<p>[[Ta-ki-ta · 3|Konnakol – Ta Ki Ta · 3]] · [[Ta-ka-di-mi · 4|Konnakol – Ta Ka Di Mi · 4]] · [[Ta-din-gi-na-tom · 5|Konnakol – Ta Din Gi Na Tom · 5]] · [[Ta-ki-ta + Ta-ka-di-mi · 7|Konnakol – Ta Ki Ta Ta Ka Di Mi · 7]]</p>
<p>''Speak the syllables yourself!'' The ABC player sounds percussion notes, not a synthesized human voice. The best way to learn accents and pronunciation is to listen to videos and live musicians.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>2 · Combine the groups</h2>
<p>[[3+5 over a 4/4 pulse|Konnakol – 3 plus 5 over fire slag]] · [[Miśra Cāpu · 7/8 melody with chord symbols|Konnakol – Miśra Cāpu · 7/8 melodi]]</p>
<p>Groups can be placed inside a steady tāla and altered without changing the underlying pulse. Students can clap, sing and eventually notate their own variations.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>3 · Melodies and accompaniment</h2>
<p>[[Mohanam-inspired melody in Ādi-tāla|Indien – Mohanam-inspireret · Adi tala]] · [[Rūpaka-inspired three-beat melody|Indien – Rupaka · tre pulsslag]]</p>
<p>Select the new <strong>India-inspired educational styles</strong> in Accompaniment. These are intentionally MIDI-based models, not authentic Indian instrument recordings. The Western chord symbols are provided for comparison and composition.</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>4 · Ragas throughout the day</h2>
<p>North Indian Hindustani music traditionally associates some ragas with particular times of day. South Indian konnakol and tāla belong to a different pedagogical tradition.</p>
<p>[[Meet Bhairav in the morning and Yaman in the evening|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Raga]]</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>Listen to real performers</h2>
<p><strong>Konnakol duet – V Shivapriya and BR Somashekar Jois</strong>. Listen to spoken rhythmic phrases and watch how their hands mark the recurring pulse.</p>
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/iurhjlBum0o" title="Konnakol duet – MadRasana Unplugged" width="560" height="315" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="max-width:100%;border:0;aspect-ratio:16/9"></iframe>
<p>[[Open the video on YouTube|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iurhjlBum0o]] – also useful if embedding is blocked in local iPad/Quine views.</p>
<p><strong>Raga Yaman – an introduction by Bidisha Ghosh</strong>. A North Indian melodic lesson, distinct from the South Indian konnakol work.</p>
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/FTXP7niGcOs" title="Raga Yaman – introduction with Bidisha Ghosh" width="560" height="315" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="max-width:100%;border:0;aspect-ratio:16/9"></iframe>
<p>[[Open the Yaman video on YouTube|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FTXP7niGcOs]]</p></div>
<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>Task: From rhythm to your own melody</h2><ol>
<li>Listen to a performer and speak the syllables along with them.</li>
<li>Clap the pulse while playing the rhythmic exercise.</li>
<li>Copy the ABC tiddler and change 3+5 into 5+3.</li>
<li>Play a melody using your chosen rhythm and open the keyboard.</li>
<li>Write a short practice log and, if you wish, publish your version as a HUWiki Site player.</li>
</ol></div>
<nav class="huw-music-bottomnav">[[Music Edition|HUWiki Musik – Start]] · [[Rhythm|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Rytmik]] · [[Ragas|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Raga]] · [[Sources|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Indiske kilder]]</nav></div>

<div class="huw-music-panel"><h2>Drone · your own Sa</h2><p>Start an independent drone in the player even if accompaniment is disabled. Choose Sa, Sa–Pa or Sa–Ma and set the key, timbre and volume in the mixer. The drone remains on the same pitch when chord symbols change. Select <strong>Stop drone</strong> to silence it.</p><p>The tanpura and shruti sounds are synthesized teaching approximations. The music examples likewise use General MIDI instruments; the tabla patterns are not authentic tabla samples.</p></div>

!!! Instrumentation · musical principles (v0.3.10)

In traditional Indian classical music, a melody is usually performed over a fixed ''Sa'' (sometimes supported by ''Pa'' or ''Ma'') and a rhythmic cycle (//tāla//). The Indian study accompaniments therefore use ''no Western bass line or changing chords by default''. All sounds are educational syntheses and General MIDI approximations; real tanpura, shruti box, tabla and mridangam instruments are much richer.

''Tanpura:'' plucked strings and harmonics, often Pa–Sa–Sa–Sa. ''Shruti box:'' a small bellows-powered instrument with metal reeds sustaining Sa/Pa or Sa/Ma. ''Mridangam:'' South Indian drum used in Carnatic music, Ādi-tāla and konnakol. ''Tabla:'' drums mainly associated with North Indian music. Harmonium can support a melody; it is not automatically a Western chord machine.

For ''Western harmonization'', choose the explicit fusion style or //Custom mix//. The drone itself never changes Sa with the chords and stops when you press Stop or choose a different score.

Ragaer · melodier gennem døgnet

I den ''nordindiske hindustanske tradition'' forbindes bestemte ragaer traditionelt med tider på dagen. En raga er mere end en skala: der er karakteristiske melodiske bevægelser, centrale toner, frasering, ornamenter og i nogle tilfælde særlige intonationsnuancer.

!! Begynd med to originale ABC-studier

* [[Bhairav-inspireret · morgen|Indien – Bhairav · morgenmelodi]] – hør især sænket Re og Dha.
* [[Yaman-inspireret · tidlig aften|Indien – Yaman · aftenmelodi]] – hør især hævet Ma.
* [[Mohanam-inspireret femtonemelodi|Indien – Mohanam-inspireret · Adi tala]] – sydindisk toneudvalg, men bemærk at Mohanam ikke har en universel bestemt tid på døgnet.

De tre korte melodier er nyskrevne øvestykker, ikke traditionelle raga-fremførelser. Akkompagnementets vestlige becifringer er bevidst en //sammenlignende undervisningsmodel// og ikke det traditionelle ragaakkompagnement (tanpura-drone og tala-baseret percussion).

!! Sammenlign

# Hør først melodien alene og syng tonerne.
# Åbn klaviaturet og find Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha og Ni.
# Prøv at ændre tempo og transponere: Sa flytter med til en ny grundtone.
# Lyt derpå til en rigtig udøver for at høre ornamenter og frasering, som ABC-studiet ikke gengiver.

","huwiki-text-en":"! Ragas · melodies throughout the day

In the ''North Indian Hindustani tradition'', some ragas are associated with particular times of day. A raga is more than a scale: it includes characteristic melodic gestures, important tones, phrasing, ornaments and sometimes particular shades of intonation.

!! Begin with two original ABC studies

* [[Bhairav-inspired · morning|Indien – Bhairav · morgenmelodi]] – listen especially for lowered Re and Dha.
* [[Yaman-inspired · early evening|Indien – Yaman · aftenmelodi]] – listen for raised Ma.
* [[Mohanam-inspired pentatonic melody|Indien – Mohanam-inspireret · Adi tala]] – South Indian pitch material; Mohanam does not have one universally prescribed time of day.

These three short melodies are newly composed exercises, not traditional raga performances. Their Western chord symbols are intentionally a //comparative teaching model//, not traditional raga accompaniment (tanpura drone and tāla-based percussion).

!! Compare

# Listen to the melody alone and sing the notes.
# Open the keyboard and find Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha and Ni.
# Change the tempo and transpose: Sa moves to a new tonic.
# Then listen to a skilled performer to hear ornaments and phrasing that the ABC study does not reproduce.

<h2>Listen to real performers</h2>
<p><strong>Konnakol duet – V Shivapriya and BR Somashekar Jois</strong>. Listen to spoken phrases and watch the hands mark a cyclic pulse.</p>

</div>

!!! Instrumentation · musical principles (v0.3.10)

In traditional Indian classical music, a melody is typically played over a fixed ''Sa'' (possibly supported by ''Pa'' or ''Ma'') and a rhythmic cycle (//tāla//). Indian teaching accompaniments consequently have ''no Western bass and no changing chords by default''. The sounds are educational syntheses and GM approximations; real tanpura, shruti box, tabla and mridangam are far richer.

''Tanpura:'' plucked strings and overtones, often Pa–Sa–Sa–Sa. ''Shruti box:'' a bellows-powered small instrument with metal reeds sustaining Sa/Pa or Sa/Ma. ''Mridangam:'' a South Indian drum used for Carnatic music, Ādi-tāla and konnakol. ''Tabla:'' percussion mainly associated with North Indian music. A harmonium can support a melodic line; it does not automatically play Western chord progressions.

For ''Western harmonization'', choose the explicit fusion style or //Custom mix//. The drone does not change Sa when chords change and stops when you press Stop or choose a new score.

Biblioteker · Indisk musik og konvertering til ABC

Vi har ''ikke fundet et stort kurateret indisk ABC-arkiv'' svarende til Balkanbiblioteket. Indiske noder findes mest som sargam/swara eller i særlige indiske dataformater.

* [[MusicSheets · hindustanske ragaer og vestlige noder|https://musicsheets.site/]] – sammenstillet sargam/staff og rytmiske forløb.
* [[Sargam Sikho · sange i sargam|https://www.sargamsikho.in/]] – stort katalog (ikke ABC-kode).
* [[CompMusic Carnatic Kriti Dataset|https://compmusic.upf.edu/carnatic-kriti-dataset]] – maskinlæsbare YAML-notationer fra sydindisk kompositionsrepertoire; licenser og adgang kontrolleres før genbrug.
* [[Kpnotes · Sargam til ABC konverter|https://kpnotes.com/tools/abc-converter/]] – nyttig reference til en kommende HUWiki-importfunktion.
* [[SwaralipiXML|https://indic-music.github.io/swaralipixml.html]] – særligt udvekslingsformat for indisk nodeskrift.
* [[Algorithmic Patterns in Konnakol|https://algorithmicpattern.org/patterns-in-konnakol/]] – notation, gennemgange og videoeksempel.

''Fremtidig HUWiki-import:'' Bevar original sargam som separat felt sammen med raga, tala, Sa-grundtone, ornamenter og ophav. Opret eventuelt en vestlig ABC-visning som et supplement, ikke en erstatning.

[[Til Konnakol-værkstedet|HUWiki Musiklaboratorium – Indien]]","huwiki-text-en":"! Libraries · Indian music and conversion to ABC

We have ''not found a large curated Indian ABC archive'' comparable to the Balkan library. Indian notation is more commonly available as sargam/swara or in specialized Indian data formats.

* [[MusicSheets · Hindustani ragas and Western notation|https://musicsheets.site/]] – sargam and Western staff notation with rhythmic examples.
* [[Sargam Sikho · songs in sargam|https://www.sargamsikho.in/]] – large catalogue (not ABC code).
* [[CompMusic Carnatic Kriti Dataset|https://compmusic.upf.edu/carnatic-kriti-dataset]] – machine-readable YAML notation from the South Indian repertoire; review licences and access before reuse.
* [[Kpnotes · sargam-to-ABC converter|https://kpnotes.com/tools/abc-converter/]] – useful reference for a future HUWiki importer.
* [[SwaralipiXML|https://indic-music.github.io/swaralipixml.html]] – specialized exchange format for Indian music notation.
* [[Algorithmic Patterns in Konnakol|https://algorithmicpattern.org/patterns-in-konnakol/]] – notation, explanations and video examples.

''Future HUWiki import:'' Keep the original sargam in a separate field, along with raga, tāla, Sa tonic, ornaments and provenance. Optionally add a Western ABC view as a supplement, not as a replacement.

Indien

Dette modul kræver ABC-pluginet. Musik-pluginet er valgfrit for ABC-nodearkene.
